te.lib:h-adwamuha: The deeds most beloved to Allah are those done most consistently, even if they are few.
te.lib:h-haqq-nafs: Your Lord has a right over you, your soul has a right over you, and your family has a right over you; so give each one who has a right their due.
te.lib:h-nimatan: There are two blessings in which many people are deceived: health and free time.
te.lib:h-ightanim: Take advantage of five before five: your youth before your old age, your health before your illness, your wealth before your poverty, your free time before your busyness, and your life before your death.
te.lib:h-muamin-qawi: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both. Strive for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not give up. If something befalls you, do not say: “If only I had done such and such, it would have been so and so,” but say: “Allah has decreed, and what He wills He does,” for “if only” opens the door to the work of Satan.
te.lib:h-ihfadh: O boy, I will teach you some words: Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the whole nation gathered together to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with what Allah had already written for you; and if they gathered together to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with what Allah had already written against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.
te.lib:h-yassiru: Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not drive people away.
te.lib:h-ihsan: Verily Allah has prescribed excellence in everything…
te.lib:h-makarim: I was sent only to perfect good character.
te.lib:h-ahsanukum-khuluqan: Indeed, the most beloved of you to me and the nearest to me in seating on the Day of Resurrection are those of you with the best character.
te.lib:h-kibr: No one who has an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise. A man said: “A man likes his clothes to be fine and his sandals to be fine.” He said: “Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.”
te.lib:h-tawadau: Allah has revealed to me that you should be humble, so that no one boasts over another and no one oppresses another.
te.lib:h-nasiha: “The religion is sincere counsel.” We said: “To whom?” He said: “To Allah, His Book, His Messenger, and to the leaders of the Muslims and their common people.”
te.lib:h-munkar: Whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; and if he cannot, then with his heart — and that is the weakest of faith.
te.lib:h-sabaa-yuzilluhum: Seven people Allah will shade with His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His… a young man who grew up in the worship of Allah… and a man who is called by a woman of status and beauty and says: “I fear Allah”…
te.lib:h-man-taraka: You will never give up anything for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah will replace it for you with something better.
te.lib:h-man-la-yarham: Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.
te.sit:taif:0: ‘A'ishah asked the Prophet ﷺ: “Have you encountered a day harder than the day of Uhud?” He said: “I suffered much from your people, and the hardest of it was on the day of al-‘Aqabah, when I presented myself to Ibn ‘Abd Yalil and he did not respond to what I wanted. I left, overwhelmed with grief, and did not recover until I was at Qarn al-Tha‘alib. There I found a cloud shading me, and in it was Jibril. He called me and said: ‘Allah has heard what your people said to you, and He has sent you the Angel of the Mountains so that you may order him to do whatever you wish to them.’ The Angel of the Mountains called me, greeted me and said: ‘If you wish, I will bring the two mountains together upon them.’” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No; rather I hope that Allah will bring forth from their descendants people who will worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him.”
te.sit:jabdha-arabi:0: Anas ibn Malik said: I was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was wearing a Najrani cloak with a thick border. A bedouin caught up with him and pulled him by his cloak so violently that I saw the side of the neck of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marked by the border of the cloak from the force of the pull. Then he said: “O Muhammad, order that I be given some of the wealth of Allah that you have.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to him and laughed, and then ordered that he be given something.
te.sit:bawl-arabi:0: Abu Hurayrah said: A bedouin stood up and urinated in the mosque, and the people rushed at him. The Prophet ﷺ said to them: “Leave him, and pour a bucket of water over his urine. You have been sent to make things easy, not to make them difficult.”
te.sit:tifl-hijr:0: Umm Qays bint Mihsan brought her young son, who had not yet started eating food, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat him in his lap, and the child urinated on his garment. He called for water, sprinkled it over the place, and did not wash it.
te.sit:khidmat-anas:0: Anas ibn Malik said: I served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years. He never once said “uff” to me, and he never said about anything I had done: “Why did you do it?”, nor about anything I had not done: “Why did you not do it?”
te.sit:la-taghdab:0: Abu Hurayrah narrated that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: “Advise me.” He said: “Do not become angry.” The man repeated his request several times, and each time he said: “Do not become angry.”
te.sit:laysa-shadid:0: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The strong one is not the one who overcomes people by wrestling; the strong one is the one who controls himself when angry.”
te.sit:adl-fatima:0: ‘A'ishah narrated that Quraysh were worried about the woman who had stolen… The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “What destroyed those before you was that when a noble person among them stole, they let him go, and when a weak person among them stole, they carried out the prescribed punishment on him. By the One in whose hand is my soul, if Fatimah the daughter of Muhammad were to steal, I would cut off her hand.”
te.sit:hudaybiyyah:0: Sahih al-Bukhari reports the story of the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah at length, including ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab's questioning of the Prophet ﷺ about the terms of the treaty, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq's reply that he must hold fast to the Prophet's command and trust that he would never lose what his Lord had entrusted to him.
te.sit:zayd-ibn-sana:0: Zayd ibn Sa‘nah narrated the story of his acceptance of Islam after he deliberately tested the forbearance of the Prophet ﷺ while demanding repayment of a debt, and found in him what he had been looking for among the signs of prophethood described in the books of the People of the Book: “His forbearance outstrips his anger, and the more harshly he is treated, the more forbearing he becomes.”
te.sit:hatib-baltaa:0: ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent three of us to intercept a woman carrying a letter from Hatib ibn Abi Balta‘ah to Quraysh. When the letter was brought, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Hatib, what is this?” He said: “Do not be hasty with me, O Messenger of Allah…” ‘Umar said: “Let me strike the neck of this hypocrite.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “He took part in Badr; and how do you know? Perhaps Allah looked at the people of Badr and said: ‘Do as you wish, for I have forgiven you.’”
te.sit:wafat-ibrahim:0: Anas ibn Malik narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to his son Ibrahim while he was breathing his last, and the eyes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to shed tears. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf said to him: “Even you, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “O Ibn ‘Awf, it is mercy.” Then he wept more and said: “The eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord. O Ibrahim, we are truly saddened by your parting.”
te.sit:mihnat-ahlih:0: Al-Aswad ibn Yazid said: I asked ‘A'ishah: “What did the Prophet ﷺ do in his house?” She said: “He used to be in the service of his family — meaning he helped his family — and when the time for prayer came, he went out to pray.”
te.sit:mihnat-ahlih:1: ‘A'ishah was asked: “What did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do in his house?” She said: “He used to sew his garment, mend his sandals, and work in his house as any of you works in his house.”
te.sit:kaab-ibn-malik:0: From the long hadith of Ka‘b ibn Malik about staying behind from Tabuk: When I told the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the truth about myself, he said: “As for this one, he has spoken the truth; so get up until Allah decides about you.” And the Prophet ﷺ ordered the people to shun us until Allah revealed our repentance.
te.sit:istikhara:0: Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us istikharah in all matters as he taught us a surah of the Quran. He would say: “When one of you is concerned about a matter, let him pray two units of prayer other than the obligatory prayer, then say: ‘O Allah, I seek Your guidance through Your knowledge, and I seek ability through Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty. You are able and I am not; You know and I do not; and You are the Knower of the unseen…’ Then let him mention his need.”
te.sit:neighbors:0: ‘A'ishah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Jibril kept enjoining me to treat the neighbour well, until I thought he would make him an heir.”
te.sit:sighar-kibar:0: Abu Hurayrah and Ibn ‘Abbas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “He is not one of us who does not show mercy to our young and respect our elders.”
te.sit:husn-dhann:0: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not look for one another's faults, do not spy on one another, do not compete with one another, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, and do not turn your backs on one another. Be, O servants of Allah, brothers.”
te.sit:thumama:0: Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet ﷺ sent some horsemen towards Najd, and they brought a man from Banu Hanifah called Thumamah ibn Uthal, and tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ came out to him and said: “What do you have, O Thumamah?” He said: “I have good, O Muhammad…” He left him until the day after next, then said: “Release Thumamah.” He went to a palm grove near the mosque, bathed, then entered the mosque and said: “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”
te.sit:hunayn-ansar:0: ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn ‘Asim said: When Allah gave His Messenger the spoils on the day of Hunayn, he distributed them among those whose hearts were to be reconciled and gave nothing to the Ansar, and it was as if they felt hurt that they had not received what others received. So he addressed them and said: “O Ansar, did I not find you astray and Allah guided you through me, divided and Allah united you through me, and poor and Allah enriched you through me?… Are you not pleased that the people go away with sheep and camels while you go back to your homes with the Messenger of Allah? Were it not for the emigration, I would have been one of the Ansar.”
te.sit:khutbat-wadaa:0: Abu Nadrah said: Someone who heard the sermon of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the middle of the days of Tashriq told me that he said: “O people, your Lord is one and your father is one. There is no superiority of an Arab over a non-Arab, nor of a non-Arab over an Arab, nor of a red-skinned person over a black person, nor of a black person over a red-skinned person, except by piety.”
te.sit:numan-bashir:0: Al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir narrated that his father brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “I have given this son of mine a slave.” He asked: “Have you given each of your children the like of this?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then take it back.”
te.sit:dog-water:0: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “While a man was walking along a road he became very thirsty. He found a well, went down into it and drank, then came out. There he saw a dog panting and eating the moist earth out of thirst. The man said: ‘This dog has become as thirsty as I was.’ So he went down into the well, filled his leather sock with water, held it in his mouth until he climbed up, and gave the dog water to drink. Allah thanked him for it and forgave him.” They said: “O Messenger of Allah, is there a reward for us in (serving) animals?” He said: “In every living creature there is a reward.”
te.sit:hospitality:0: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not harm his neighbour; whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honour his guest; and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should say what is good or keep silent.”
te.sit:sila-rahim:0: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The one who maintains ties of kinship is not the one who merely reciprocates; rather, the one who maintains ties is the one who, when his relatives cut him off, keeps the ties with them.”
te.sit:jewish-boy-sick:0: Anas ibn Malik said: A Jewish boy used to serve the Prophet ﷺ, and he fell ill. The Prophet ﷺ went to visit him, sat by his head and said to him: “Accept Islam.” The boy looked at his father, who was with him, and he said: “Obey Abu al-Qasim.” So he accepted Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ went out saying: “Praise be to Allah who saved him from the Fire.”
